purpose: libtiff is a library for reading, writing, and manipulating TIFF image files.

functions.TIFFWriteEncodedTile: `TIFFWriteEncodedTile` writes one tile’s encoded data to a TIFF. Use it only for writable tiled images, with a valid `tile` index and `data/cc` matching the tile payload. It checks bounds/buffer setup, reserves write space, and returns `-1` on error.
functions.TIFFSetWarningHandlerExt: `TIFFSetWarningHandlerExt` sets libtiff’s extended warning callback and returns the previous one. Use it to install or replace a `TIFFErrorHandlerExt`; pass `NULL` to disable warnings. It has no other logic beyond swapping the global handler.
functions.TIFFComputeTile: `TIFFComputeTile` maps pixel coords `(x,y,z)` plus sample `s` to the tile index in a tiled TIFF. Use it to locate which tile contains a given point. If tile dims are unset/invalid, it falls back to image dims; for 2D images `z` is forced to 0. Separate-planar images include `s` in the index.
functions.TIFFIsBigEndian: `TIFFIsBigEndian(TIFF*)` checks a TIFF handle’s header magic to tell whether the file was written in big-endian byte order. Use it on a valid `TIFF*`; it returns nonzero if big-endian, 0 otherwise. It’s a simple query, not a conversion.
functions.TIFFRasterScanlineSize: Returns the raster scanline byte size for a TIFF image. Use it to allocate/read one scanline of raster data. It calls `TIFFRasterScanlineSize64()` then safely casts to `tmsize_t`; if the size can’t fit, the cast helper handles the error.
functions.TIFFRawStripSize64: Returns the raw byte size of a given strip. Use it to query compressed/on-disk strip size. If `TIFFGetStrileByteCount()` returns 0, it reports an error and returns `(uint64_t)-1` as invalid.
functions.TIFFGetSeekProc: `TIFFGetSeekProc` returns the current seek callback stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to inspect which low-level seek function a TIFF handle is using. It doesn’t seek itself; it just returns `tif->tif_seekproc` (or NULL if unset).
functions.TIFFCleanup: `TIFFCleanup` is the internal teardown routine for a `TIFF*`: it flushes pending writes if not `O_RDONLY`, calls the format-specific cleanup hook, frees directory/client-info state, and releases owned buffers/mappings. Use it when closing/destroying a TIFF handle; don’t use after the handle is invalid.
functions.TIFFReadRawTile: Reads a tile’s raw encoded bytes into `buf` without decoding. Use with a valid `tile` index and `size` as buffer capacity; if `size` is -1 or smaller than the tile bytecount, it reads the full bytecount. Returns bytes read, or -1 on error/out-of-range/unsupported raw access.
functions.TIFFStripSize: `TIFFStripSize` returns the byte size of one strip for a TIFF image. Use it with a valid `TIFF*`; it wraps `TIFFStripSize64()` and casts to `tmsize_t`. If the 64-bit size can’t fit in `tmsize_t`, the cast helper handles that case.
functions.TIFFFileName: `TIFFFileName(TIFF*)` returns the TIFF handle’s stored file name string (`tif->tif_name`). Use it to query the name associated with an open `TIFF*`. It does no validation or I/O; it simply returns the pointer held in the object.
functions.TIFFUnlinkDirectory: `TIFFUnlinkDirectory` removes a directory from a TIFF file’s directory chain. Use it only on writable TIFFs; it returns 0 and reports an error if the file is read-only. It walks to the previous directory, patches its next-link, and behavior depends on classic TIFF vs BigTIFF offsets.
functions._TIFFrealloc: `_TIFFrealloc` is a thin libtiff wrapper around `realloc()`. Use it to resize a heap block previously allocated by malloc/realloc-like routines. It returns the new pointer on success, or `NULL` on failure; `p` may be `NULL` to allocate fresh memory.
functions.TIFFFreeDirectory: `TIFFFreeDirectory` frees/reset the current `TIFF` directory’s allocated field data and custom tag values. Use it to clean up a directory before reusing/destroying the `TIFF`; it clears field bits, frees owned buffers, and resets allocation state.
functions.TIFFWriteCustomDirectory: `TIFFWriteCustomDirectory` is a thin wrapper around `TIFFWriteDirectorySec`. It writes the current TIFF directory as a “custom” directory, storing the new directory offset in `*pdiroff`. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and non-NULL `uint64_t*`. It returns the underlying write status.
functions.TIFFReverseBits: `TIFFReverseBits` reverses the bit order of each byte in a buffer in place. Call it with a valid `uint8_t*` and byte count `n`; it processes 8 bytes at a time, then any remainder. No-op if `n<=0`.
functions.TIFFNumberOfTiles: Returns the total tile count for the TIFF, using tile size and image dimensions; if tile dims are unset (-1), it falls back to full image size. Use after directory setup. Returns 0 if any tile dim is 0; multiplies by samples/pixel for PLANARCONFIG_SEPARATE.
functions.TIFFIsByteSwapped: `TIFFIsByteSwapped()` reports whether a `TIFF*` was opened with byte-swapping enabled for endianness conversion. Call it on a valid `TIFF` handle; it returns nonzero if `TIFF_SWAB` is set, otherwise 0.
functions.TIFFVTileSize: `TIFFVTileSize` is a thin wrapper that computes a tile’s byte size for `nrows` via `TIFFVTileSize64`, then safely casts to `tmsize_t`. Use it when you need the size of a tile buffer. If the 64-bit size won’t fit in `tmsize_t`, the cast handles the overflow case.
functions.TIFFSetFileno: `TIFFSetFileno` sets the TIFF handle’s underlying file descriptor to `fd` and returns the previous descriptor. Use it to replace/rebind the I/O target for an existing `TIFF*`. It does no validation or I/O; it just updates `tif->tif_fd`.
functions.TIFFRawStripSize: Returns the raw byte size of a strip. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and strip index to know compressed/on-disk strip size. It calls `TIFFRawStripSize64`; on error it returns `-1`, and if the 64-bit size overflows `tmsize_t`, it reports “Integer overflow” and returns `0`.
functions.TIFFReadEXIFDirectory: `TIFFReadEXIFDirectory` reads an EXIF IFD from the TIFF at `diroff` using libtiff’s EXIF field definitions. Call it with a valid `TIFF*` and directory offset. It returns the result of `TIFFReadCustomDirectory` (success/failure).
functions.TIFFGetConfiguredCODECs: Returns a heap-allocated array of configured codecs. Use it to enumerate registered + built-in codecs that are enabled. On alloc failure it frees partial data and returns NULL. Caller should free the returned array.
functions.TIFFFieldName: `TIFFFieldName` is a simple accessor that returns a TIFF field’s name string (`field_name`). Use it with a valid `TIFFField*` to get the field’s human-readable name. It does no checking or allocation and just returns the stored pointer.
functions._TIFFmemset:
`_TIFFmemset` is a thin libtiff wrapper around `memset`. Use it to fill `c` bytes at `p` with byte value `v`. It behaves like `memset`; `c` is cast to `size_t`, so it performs no extra checks or special handling.
Not directly misused by the caller; it crashes because TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit computed a pointer into insufficient caller-provided storage. Prevent this by ensuring the destination buffer passed indirectly to _TIFFmemset via TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit is valid and sufficiently sized.
Yes, this is misuse. `_TIFFmemset(p, v, c)` writes exactly `c` bytes to `p`; call it only when `p` points to a valid buffer of at least `c` bytes. In this case, use the actual allocated size for `c` rather than the intended size `s2` if allocation was smaller. Always validate that `c >= 0` and `c <= allocated_size` before calling.
functions.TIFFDefaultStripSize: `TIFFDefaultStripSize` is a thin wrapper that delegates to `tif->tif_defstripsize`. Use it to get the library’s default recommended strip size for a TIFF handle, optionally influenced by `request`. Behavior depends entirely on the TIFF object’s installed callback.
functions.TIFFClientdata: `TIFFClientdata(TIFF*)` returns the client-supplied handle stored in a `TIFF` object. Use it when you need the original I/O context passed to `TIFFClientOpen`. It simply returns `tif->tif_clientdata`; no extra logic or error handling.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfDouble: Swaps byte order of an array of `double` in place. Use it on `n` 8-byte doubles when TIFF data endianness differs from the host. It asserts `sizeof(double)==8`; `n==0` does nothing.
functions.TIFFIsCODECConfigured: Checks whether a TIFF codec is actually configured/usable. Call it with a compression scheme ID. It returns 1 only if `TIFFFindCODEC()` finds a codec and its `init` is not `NULL` or `NotConfigured`; otherwise 0.
functions.TIFFFieldWriteCount: `TIFFFieldWriteCount` returns a TIFF field’s declared write-count (`field_writecount`). Use it to query how many values a field expects when writing tags. It simply returns that stored count; no validation or special-case behavior.
functions.TIFFFieldWithName: `TIFFFieldWithName` looks up a TIFF tag definition by its name in a `TIFF*` handle. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and tag name string. It returns the matching `TIFFField*`, or `NULL` and logs an internal error if the name is unknown.
functions.TIFFScanlineSize: Returns the byte size of one image scanline for `tif`. Use it to allocate/read/write a row buffer. It calls `TIFFScanlineSize64()` then casts to `tmsize_t`; if the size can’t fit, the cast helper handles/report it.
functions.TIFFCIELabToXYZ: Converts CIE L*a*b* to XYZ using `TIFFCIELabToRGB` white-point refs (`X0/Y0/Z0`). Input `l` is 0–255 mapped to 0–100; `a`,`b` are signed offsets. Writes `X,Y,Z` via pointers. Uses linear branch for low L and cubic for others.
functions.TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit:
Initializes a `TIFFYCbCrToRGB` converter for YCbCr→RGB lookup tables. Pass the struct plus luma and refBlackWhite arrays. It sets clamp/table pointers and precomputes conversion tables; use before any YCbCr-to-RGB conversion.
Misused. Do not pass a standalone stack-allocated TIFFYCbCrToRGB object. This function expects a memory block large enough for the TIFFYCbCrToRGB struct plus the lookup-table storage it lays out immediately after the struct. Allocate a contiguous buffer of at least roundup(sizeof(TIFFYCbCrToRGB), sizeof(long)) + space for clamptab/YCbCr tables, cast it to TIFFYCbCrToRGB*, then call TIFFYCbCrToRGBInit() on that buffer. Alternatively, use higher-level libtiff RGBA conversion APIs that manage internal storage for you.
functions.TIFFGetVersion: `TIFFGetVersion()` returns a pointer to libtiff’s built-in version string (`TIFFVersion`). Use it to query the library version at runtime. It takes no arguments, has no failure cases in this code, and simply returns the same constant string each call.
functions._TIFFmemcpy: `_TIFFmemcpy` is a thin libtiff wrapper around `memcpy`. Use it to copy `c` bytes from `s` to `d`. It has the same behavior/requirements as `memcpy`: source and destination must not overlap; `c` is cast to `size_t`.
functions.TIFFWriteRawTile: `TIFFWriteRawTile` appends raw, already-encoded tile data to a TIFF tile. Use it only when writing tiled images and `tile < td_nstrips`; otherwise it errors and returns `-1`. On success it returns `cc`, else `-1`.
functions.TIFFSwabLong8: `TIFFSwabLong8` byte-swaps a 64-bit unsigned integer in place, converting between little- and big-endian order. Pass a valid `uint64_t*`; it always swaps all 8 bytes and assumes `sizeof(uint64_t)==8`.
functions.TIFFCreateCustomDirectory:
Creates a new “custom” TIFF directory: resets to default state, then installs the app’s field definitions via `_TIFFSetupFields()`. Use it before writing/using a nonstandard directory. It clears offsets/row/strip state and always returns 0.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Do not pass NULL as the infoarray argument. Invoke TIFFCreateCustomDirectory(tif, infoarray) only with a valid, fully initialized TIFFFieldArray* that describes the custom directory fields, including a valid fields pointer and correct count. If no custom field definitions are needed, avoid calling this API and use standard directory creation APIs instead. Also validate pointers before calling and handle a failure return defensively.
functions.TIFFReadGPSDirectory: `TIFFReadGPSDirectory` reads a GPS IFD from a TIFF at `diroff`. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and directory offset. It gets the GPS field definitions via `_TIFFGetGpsFields()` and delegates to `TIFFReadCustomDirectory()`, returning that result.
functions.uv_encode: Encodes CIE u′,v′ into a packed index for the UV table. Use it with `u,v` and rounding mode `em`. If coords are outside the valid UV grid/range, it falls back to `oog_encode(u,v)`; otherwise returns the row’s cumulative offset plus column index.
functions.TIFFCurrentTile: `TIFFCurrentTile` returns the current tile index stored in `tif->tif_curtile`. Use it after tile-based I/O to query which tile the `TIFF*` is positioned on. It just returns the cached value; no validation or side effects.
functions.LogL16fromY: Converts a Y luminance value to 16-bit LogL encoding. Use with a valid `Y` and rounding mode `em`. Large +Y saturates to `0x7fff`, large -Y to `0xffff`, near-zero returns `0`, otherwise it maps `log2(|Y|)` into the 16-bit range.
functions.TIFFSetSubDirectory: `TIFFSetSubDirectory` sets `tif_nextdiroff` to a given IFD offset, resets the directory counter/seen-list to avoid IFD loops, then reads that directory via `TIFFReadDirectory()`. Use it to jump to a specific subdirectory; it returns that read’s status.
functions.TIFFFdOpen: `TIFFFdOpen` opens a TIFF stream from an existing OS file descriptor. Use it when you already have `fd`; it wraps it with libtiff I/O callbacks via `TIFFClientOpen`. On success it returns `TIFF*` and stores `fd` in `tif_fd`; otherwise returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFFlush: `TIFFFlush` writes pending image data and, if needed, updates the directory. Use it after writing/updating a TIFF to force buffered data out. In `O_RDONLY` it’s a no-op success. In `O_RDWR`, it may rewrite only strip/tile maps or the full directory; failures return 0.
functions.TIFFVStripSize: `TIFFVStripSize` returns the byte size of a strip for `nrows` rows. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and row count. It delegates to `TIFFVStripSize64`, then casts to `tmsize_t`; if the size won’t fit, the cast helper handles the error.
functions.TIFFGetStrileByteCount: Returns the byte count for a given strile (strip/tile) in a TIFF. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and strile index. It simply forwards to `TIFFGetStrileByteCountWithErr(..., NULL)`, so any error reporting is suppressed and the returned value reflects that helper’s result.
functions.TIFFSwabDouble: `TIFFSwabDouble` byte-swaps an 8-byte `double` in place. Use it on a valid `double*` when converting between opposite-endian TIFF data and host order. It simply reverses the 8 bytes; `assert` expects `sizeof(double)==8`.
functions.TIFFVSetField: `TIFFVSetField` is the varargs-backed tag setter used internally by libtiff. Call it with a `TIFF*`, tag ID, and `va_list`; it forwards to the format-specific `vsetfield` handler only if `OkToChangeTag` allows the tag. Returns 0 if disallowed, else handler result.
functions.TIFFVStripSize64: Returns the byte size of a strip for `nrows` rows. Use `nrows==(uint32_t)-1` to mean full image height. For packed, non-upsampled YCbCr contiguous data it accounts for subsampling/round-up; invalid `SamplesPerPixel` returns 0 and logs an error.
functions.TIFFIsTiled: `TIFFIsTiled(TIFF*)` is a simple query API: it checks whether a TIFF image is stored in tiled layout. Use it after opening a TIFF to branch tile vs. strip handling. It returns nonzero if tiled, 0 otherwise.
functions.TIFFSetMode: `TIFFSetMode` simply changes a `TIFF` handle’s internal `tif_mode` and returns the previous mode. Use it on an already opened `TIFF*` to switch/read the mode value. It does no validation, I/O, or side effects beyond assignment.
functions.TIFFFieldReadCount: `TIFFFieldReadCount` is a simple accessor for a `TIFFField`’s `field_readcount`. Use it to query how many values a tag expects when read. It returns the stored count directly; no validation, conversion, or special-case handling is performed.
functions.TIFFGetMode: `TIFFGetMode` returns the current access mode stored in a `TIFF*` handle (`tif->tif_mode`). Use it after opening a TIFF to query whether the file was opened for reading, writing, etc. It does no validation or side effects; it just returns the mode value.
functions.TIFFSetErrorHandler: `TIFFSetErrorHandler` sets libtiff’s global error-reporting callback and returns the previous handler. Use it to install your own `TIFFErrorHandler`; pass `NULL` to disable handling. It affects subsequent TIFF errors globally.
functions.TIFFGetBitRevTable: `TIFFGetBitRevTable(reversed)` returns a lookup table for byte bit-reversal. Use it when you need to map bytes to their reversed-bit form. If `reversed` is nonzero, it returns `TIFFBitRevTable`; otherwise `TIFFNoBitRevTable` (identity table).
functions.TIFFWriteRawStrip: `TIFFWriteRawStrip` writes a raw, already-encoded strip to a TIFF. Use it with a valid strip index and byte count `cc`. It checks write mode/strip bounds; returns `-1` on error. It won’t grow separate-plane images by strips.
functions.TIFFSetWarningHandler: `TIFFSetWarningHandler` sets libtiff’s global warning callback and returns the previous one. Use it to install your own warning handler or restore an old one. Passing `NULL` disables warning reporting via the handler.
functions.TIFFFindCODEC: `TIFFFindCODEC` looks up a codec by its `scheme` ID. It searches registered codecs first, then built-in codecs. Use it to test whether a codec exists and get its `TIFFCodec*`. If no match is found, it returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFSwabFloat: `TIFFSwabFloat` byte-swaps a 4-byte `float` in place to convert endianness. Pass a valid `float*`; it swaps bytes 0↔3 and 1↔2. It assumes `sizeof(float)==4` and only works correctly for 4-byte floats.
functions.TIFFGetFieldDefaulted: `TIFFGetFieldDefaulted` is a varargs wrapper for `TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted`. Use it to read a tag from `tif`, getting the tag’s stored value or a default if the tag isn’t set. It returns the underlying success status from `TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted`.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfFloat: `TIFFSwabArrayOfFloat` byte-swaps `n` 4-byte floats in place. Use it on float arrays when TIFF data endianness differs from the host. It assumes `sizeof(float)==4`; with `n<=0` it does nothing.
functions.TIFFSetWriteOffset: `TIFFSetWriteOffset` directly sets `tif->tif_curoff` to the given file offset. It’s a low-level state setter for TIFF write position; use it only when you need to manually control the next write offset. It has no validation or side effects.
functions._TIFFfree: `_TIFFfree` is a thin libtiff wrapper around `free()`. Use it to release heap memory allocated by libtiff or compatible allocators. It accepts `NULL` safely (no effect). It does not resize or validate the block; it simply frees the pointer passed in.
functions.TIFFWriteBufferSetup: `TIFFWriteBufferSetup` sets/allocates the TIFF output raw-data buffer. Pass `bp`+`size` to use your buffer, or `size=-1` to auto-size and malloc (min 8KB, +10% margin). It frees any prior owned buffer; on alloc failure it reports error and returns 0.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfShort: `TIFFSwabArrayOfShort` byte-swaps an array of 16-bit values in place. Use it on `wp` with `n` elements when TIFF data endianness differs from host order. It loops over each `uint16_t`; `n<=0` does nothing.
functions._TIFFmemcmp: `_TIFFmemcmp` is a thin wrapper around `memcmp` for libtiff. Use it to compare `c` bytes from `p1` and `p2`. It returns the same as `memcmp`: `0` if equal, `<0` or `>0` if they differ.
functions.TIFFTileSize64: `TIFFTileSize64` returns the size in bytes of one tile as a `uint64_t`. It’s a convenience wrapper around `TIFFVTileSize64(tif, tif->tif_dir.td_tilelength)`, so use it on a valid `TIFF*` after tile parameters are set. It just computes and returns the tile size.
functions.TIFFScanlineSize64: `TIFFScanlineSize64` returns the byte size of one image row, using 64-bit math to avoid overflow on very large images. Use it after TIFF tags are set/read. It handles contig YCbCr subsampling specially; invalid tag values may trigger an error and return 0.
functions.TIFFClose: `TIFFClose` finalizes a TIFF handle: it calls `TIFFCleanup(tif)` to release libtiff resources, then invokes the file’s close callback on `tif_clientdata`. Use it once when done with a `TIFF*`; it doesn’t return a status and assumes `tif`/`closeproc` are valid.
functions.TIFFReadTile: `TIFFReadTile` reads and decodes the tile containing `(x,y,z,s)` into `buf`. Use it only after a valid read setup; it checks access and tile coords, returning `-1` on failure. On success it reads the computed encoded tile via `TIFFReadEncodedTile`.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfTriples: Swaps byte order in-place for an array of 3-byte records (“triples”): each item’s 1st and 3rd bytes are exchanged, middle byte unchanged. Use on `tp` with `n` triples. If `n<=0`, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFGetClientInfo: `TIFFGetClientInfo` looks up a client-info entry by `name` in a `TIFF*` and returns its stored `void*` data. Use it after client info has been attached to that TIFF handle. If no matching name exists, it returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFClientOpen: `TIFFClientOpen` creates a TIFF handle using caller-supplied I/O callbacks, so libtiff can read/write from custom sources (memory, network, etc.). Pass the client data and valid read/write/seek/close/size/map/unmap funcs. It returns a `TIFF*` on success, `NULL` on failure.
functions.TIFFRegisterCODEC: Registers a new compression codec in libtiff’s internal list. Use it with a scheme ID, codec name, and init callback. On success it allocates/stores the codec and returns its `TIFFCodec*`; on malloc failure it logs an error and returns `NULL`.
functions.TIFFCIELabToRGBInit: Initializes a `TIFFCIELabToRGB` converter from a `TIFFDisplay` and reference white. It copies display params, builds gamma tables/steps for Lab→RGB mapping. Use it once before conversions; it returns `int` status.
functions.TIFFUnRegisterCODEC: `TIFFUnRegisterCODEC` removes a previously registered codec from libtiff’s codec list. Call it with the same `TIFFCodec*` passed to registration. If found, it unlinks and frees it; if not, it reports an error: “not registered”.
functions.TIFFVTileSize64: Computes the byte size of a tile for `nrows` rows. Use it after tile geometry is set; returns 0 if tilewidth/length/depth are unset. Special-cases packed YCbCr contig data with subsampling, rounding up for partial blocks.
functions.TIFFFileno: `TIFFFileno(TIFF*)` returns the underlying file descriptor stored in `tif->tif_fd`. Use it when you need the OS-level fd for a TIFF handle. It does no validation or I/O; it simply returns the current descriptor value.
functions.TIFFNumberOfDirectories: Counts TIFF directories by walking the IFD chain from the header. Use it on an open `TIFF*` to get the number of directories. Returns `uint16_t`; if count exceeds 65535, it reports an error and returns 65535.
functions.TIFFSetupStrips: `TIFFSetupStrips` initializes a TIFF’s strip/tile bookkeeping and allocates `StripOffsets`/`StripByteCounts` arrays. Use it after directory fields are known, before writing/using strip data. It returns 0 on oversized or alloc-fail cases; otherwise sets counts and pointers.
functions.TIFFFieldTag: `TIFFFieldTag` is a simple accessor for a `TIFFField`’s tag value. Pass a valid, non-NULL `TIFFField*`; it returns `fip->field_tag` as a `uint32_t`. It has no side effects or special cases beyond dereferencing the pointer.
functions.TIFFIsMSB2LSB: `TIFFIsMSB2LSB(tif)` checks whether the TIFF’s FillOrder is `FILLORDER_MSB2LSB` (most-significant-bit first). Use it to query bit order before reading/writing packed data. It returns nonzero if true, 0 otherwise.
functions.TIFFLastDirectory: `TIFFLastDirectory` checks whether the current TIFF directory is the last one in the file. Use it on a valid `TIFF*` after opening/traversing directories. It returns nonzero if `tif_nextdiroff == 0`, otherwise 0.
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfLong: `TIFFSwabArrayOfLong` byte-swaps an array of 32-bit unsigned integers in place. Use it when TIFF data endianness differs from the host. It processes `n` elements, swapping each `uint32_t`; if `n<=0`, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFSwabShort: `TIFFSwabShort` byte-swaps a 16-bit `uint16_t` in place. Pass a valid pointer to one short; it swaps the two bytes regardless of host endianness. It assumes `sizeof(uint16_t)==2` and uses `assert` for that.
functions.TIFFNumberOfStrips: `TIFFNumberOfStrips()` returns the number of strip offsets/data chunks in the current image. Use it after opening/reading directory info. It computes strips from image length and RowsPerStrip; if `PLANARCONFIG_SEPARATE`, it multiplies by samples/pixel.
functions._TIFFmalloc: `_TIFFmalloc` is a thin libtiff wrapper around `malloc`. Use it to allocate `s` bytes for TIFF-internal code. If `s == 0`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns the `malloc` result, including `NULL` on allocation failure.
functions.LogL16toY: `LogL16toY` converts a 16-bit LogL sample to luminance `Y`. Use it by passing the raw 16-bit value. If the low 15 bits are 0, it returns `0.0`; otherwise it computes an exponential scale. The sign bit (`0x8000`) makes the result negative.
functions.TIFFAccessTagMethods: `TIFFAccessTagMethods()` returns a pointer to a TIFF handle’s internal `TIFFTagMethods` table. Use it to inspect or modify the tag-method callbacks for that `TIFF*`. It just returns `&tif->tif_tagmethods`; it doesn’t validate `tif` or do any extra work.
functions.TIFFForceStrileArrayWriting: `TIFFForceStrileArrayWriting()` forces writing only the strile arrays (strip/tile offsets and bytecounts) for an already-written directory. Use it after opening writable and after the directory exists. It fails for read-only files, unwritten dirs, or if other directory fields are dirty; then `TIFFRewriteDirectory()` is needed.
functions.TIFFDefaultTileSize: `TIFFDefaultTileSize` asks the TIFF codec to fill in default tile width/height via `tif->tif_deftilesize`. Call it with a valid `TIFF*` and output pointers; it writes the codec’s suggested tile size, depending on the current TIFF/codec.
functions.TIFFWriteCheck: `TIFFWriteCheck` validates that a TIFF is writable and that the write mode matches the image layout (tiles vs scanlines). Call it before writing data. It errors if opened read-only, mode mismatches, or required fields like `ImageWidth` aren’t set; otherwise it prepares write state and returns 1.
functions.TIFFFindField: Finds a TIFF field descriptor by tag, optionally matching data type. It first returns the cached `tif_foundfield` if it matches; otherwise it binary-searches `tif->tif_fields`. Returns the found `TIFFField*` or `NULL` if no fields are loaded or no match.
functions.TIFFTileRowSize64: `TIFFTileRowSize64` computes the byte size of one row within a tile. Use it on a valid `TIFF*` after directory fields are set. It returns 0 and logs an error if tile length/width is 0, or if `PLANARCONFIG_CONTIG` has 0 samples/pixel; overflow is checked via `_TIFFMultiply64`.
functions.TIFFWriteDirectory: `TIFFWriteDirectory` is a convenience API to write the current TIFF directory/IFD to the file. Use it after setting tags for the current image. It simply calls `TIFFWriteDirectorySec(tif, TRUE, TRUE, NULL)`, so it writes with the default secure/normal behavior and returns that result.
functions.TIFFGetSizeProc: `TIFFGetSizeProc(TIFF*)` returns the `TIFFSizeProc` currently stored in the `TIFF` handle (`tif->tif_sizeproc`). Use it to query the active size-callback for that TIFF object. It does no validation or side effects; it just returns the pointer, or whatever is stored there.
functions.TIFFRGBAImageBegin: `TIFFRGBAImageBegin` initializes a `TIFFRGBAImage` for RGBA reading. Call it after opening a TIFF; it validates the file via `TIFFRGBAImageOK`, sets defaults/maps, and returns 0 on invalid/unsupported input, else prepares `img` for later pixel conversion.
functions.TIFFCheckpointDirectory: `TIFFCheckpointDirectory` is for **periodically flushing the current directory state to disk** while writing a TIFF. It ensures strip arrays exist, writes the directory as a checkpoint, then updates the write offset to EOF. Use it during incremental writes; it returns `TIFFWriteDirectorySec`’s status.
functions.TIFFSetClientInfo: Stores per-TIFF client data under a string key. Call with a `TIFF*`, your `void*` payload, and a name. If the name exists, it updates the data; otherwise it creates a new entry in `tif->tif_clientinfo`.
functions.TIFFError: `TIFFError` is libtiff’s error-reporting API. Call it with a module name and printf-style message. It forwards the formatted error to the installed error handler(s); if none are set, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFReadRGBATileExt: `TIFFReadRGBATileExt` reads a tiled TIFF tile into an RGBA raster. Use it only on tiled files, and `col,row` must be the tile’s top-left corner (aligned to tile width/length). It returns 0 on invalid use/error; `stop_on_error` controls whether decoding stops on read errors.
functions.TIFFRGBAImageGet: `TIFFRGBAImageGet` is a thin dispatcher: it validates that `img->get` and `img->put.any` are set, then calls `img->get(img, raster, w, h)`. Use it only after initializing `TIFFRGBAImage`. If setup is missing, it reports an error and returns 0; otherwise it returns the underlying get result.
functions.TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted: `TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted` is a fallback getter: it first tries `TIFFVGetField`; if the tag isn’t explicitly set, it returns the directory’s default value for known tags. Use it with a `va_list` and pointers to receive values. Returns 1 on success, 0 if unsupported.
functions.LogL10toY: `LogL10toY` converts a 10-bit LogL code (`p10`) to luminance `Y` using the TIFF LogL formula. Use it with raw 10-bit LogL samples. `p10==0` returns `0.0`; otherwise it computes an exponential mapping.
functions.TIFFVGetField: `TIFFVGetField` is a varargs helper to fetch a tag’s value via `va_list`. Use it only for tags present in the TIFF and already set, unless it’s a pseudo-tag. It returns the tag-method’s result, or `0` if the tag is unknown/unset.
functions.TIFFCurrentDirOffset: `TIFFCurrentDirOffset` returns the file offset of the TIFF directory currently selected in `TIFF* tif`. Use it after opening/reading a TIFF to query where the current IFD is stored. It simply returns `tif->tif_diroff`; no extra checks or side effects.
functions.TIFFCreateEXIFDirectory: `TIFFCreateEXIFDirectory()` creates a new TIFF directory using the EXIF field set. Call it on a valid `TIFF*` before writing EXIF tags. It simply fetches the EXIF field array and delegates to `TIFFCreateCustomDirectory()`, returning that function’s status.
functions.TIFFReadScanline: Reads one scanline into `buf` for `row`/`sample`. Use after `TIFFCheckRead`-safe open; it seeks to the row, decodes into the buffer, advances to the next row, and returns `1` on success, `-1` on failure.
functions.TIFFSetErrorHandlerExt: `TIFFSetErrorHandlerExt` sets the global extended TIFF error callback and returns the previous one. Use it to install or replace a handler; pass `NULL` to disable it. It affects later TIFF errors only, not past ones.
functions.TIFFCheckTile: `TIFFCheckTile` validates tile coordinates/samples against the image directory. Use it before tile I/O to ensure `x,y,z,s` are in range. It returns 1 if valid, 0 on out-of-range and emits a TIFF error.
functions.TIFFReadRawStrip: `TIFFReadRawStrip` reads a strip’s **raw, uncompressed encoded bytes** into `buf`. Use it only with a valid `strip` index and a buffer large enough; `size` can limit bytes read, or `-1` to read the full strip. Returns byte count, or `-1` on error (bad strip, unsupported raw access, read failure).
functions.TIFFGetCloseProc: `TIFFGetCloseProc` returns the close callback currently stored in a `TIFF*` handle (`tif->tif_closeproc`). Use it to inspect which function libtiff will call when closing that TIFF object. It just returns the pointer; no side effects or error handling.
functions.TIFFTileRowSize: Returns the byte size of one tile row for a TIFF handle. Use it after the TIFF is set up to size row buffers or iterate tile data. It calls `TIFFTileRowSize64()` and casts to `tmsize_t`; overflow is checked via `_TIFFCastUInt64ToSSize()`.
functions.TIFFGetMapFileProc: `TIFFGetMapFileProc` returns the current file-mapping callback stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to inspect which `TIFFMapFileProc` is set for that handle. It does no mapping itself and simply returns `tif->tif_mapproc` (or whatever is currently stored).
functions.TIFFDeferStrileArrayWriting: Sets `td_deferstrilearraywriting` to delay writing strile arrays. Call it only on a writable TIFF before the directory is written. Returns 1 on success; 0 if opened read-only or the directory was already written.
functions.TIFFReadRGBATile: `TIFFReadRGBATile` is a convenience wrapper for reading one tile as an RGBA raster. Call it with a valid TIFF handle, tile origin (`col`,`row`), and a pixel buffer. It simply forwards to `TIFFReadRGBATileExt(..., 0)`, so behavior matches the extended version with default options.
functions.TIFFRGBAImageOK: Checks whether `TIFFRGBAImage` can decode this TIFF. Use it before RGBA read; on failure it returns 0 and writes a reason to `emsg`. It rejects unsupported compression, sample sizes not 1/2/4/8/16, IEEE float samples, and some photometric/channel combos.
functions.TIFFSetDirectory: Sets the current TIFF IFD to directory `dirn` by walking from the first directory. Use it before reading that directory. Returns 1 on success, 0 if traversal/read fails or dirn is past the end. Resets loop-tracking state.
functions.TIFFIsUpSampled: `TIFFIsUpSampled(TIFF*)` checks whether a TIFF handle is in an upsampled state. Use it on a valid `TIFF*` to query internal decoding/processing mode. It returns nonzero if upsampled, 0 otherwise; it just forwards to `isUpSampled(tif)`.
functions.TIFFPrintDirectory: `TIFFPrintDirectory` is a diagnostic/debug helper: it prints the current TIFF directory/tag info to a `FILE*`. Call it with an open output stream; `flags` controls formatting/details. It only reports fields present in `tif->tif_dir` and prints the directory offset.
functions.TIFFComputeStrip: Computes the strip index for a given image row, and for `PLANARCONFIG_SEPARATE`, also a sample plane. Use it to map row/sample to the TIFF strip number. If `sample` is out of range, it reports an error and returns 0.
functions.LogLuv32toXYZ: Decodes a packed 32-bit LogLuv pixel into XYZ tristimulus values. Use it with a `uint32_t` LogLuv sample and a 3-float output array. If decoded luminance `L<=0`, it returns `{0,0,0}`; otherwise it computes XYZ from luminance and chromaticity.
functions.uv_decode: Decodes a UV index `c` into the center coordinates `(u',v')`. Use with valid `0 <= c < UV_NDIVS`; on success it writes `*up,*vp` and returns `0`, otherwise returns `-1`. It binary-searches `uv_row` to map the index.
functions.TIFFGetTagListEntry: Returns the tag ID at `tag_index` from `tif->tif_dir.td_customValues`. Use it to iterate custom tags by index. If `tag_index` is <0 or >= `td_customValueCount`, it returns `(uint32_t)-1`.
functions.TIFFRewriteDirectory: `TIFFRewriteDirectory` rewrites the current directory in-place if possible. If the directory was never written (`tif_diroff==0`), it just calls `TIFFWriteDirectory`. Otherwise it clears the old directory link and updates the TIFF header so the directory can be relinked/appended. Use it after modifying tags in an existing directory. Returns 0 on error.
functions.TIFFOpen: `TIFFOpen` opens a TIFF file by name and mode, returning a `TIFF*` handle. It validates the mode via `_TIFFgetMode`; invalid mode or open failure returns `NULL` and reports an error. On success it opens the fd, then wraps it with `TIFFFdOpen`; if that fails, it closes the fd.
functions.TIFFReadDirectory: `TIFFReadDirectory` advances to the next IFD, fetches/parses it, and sets `tif->tif_nextdiroff`. Use it to iterate image directories in a TIFF. It returns 1 on success, 0 on EOF/bad offset/read failure; it also cleans prior compression state.
functions.TIFFStripSize64: `TIFFStripSize64` returns the byte size of a strip for the current TIFF, using `RowsPerStrip` capped to `ImageLength`. Use it after `TIFF*` is initialized to size/read/write strip buffers. If `RowsPerStrip > ImageLength`, it uses `ImageLength`; result comes from `TIFFVStripSize64`.
functions.TIFFRGBAImageEnd: `TIFFRGBAImageEnd` is the cleanup/destructor for a `TIFFRGBAImage`. Call it after `TIFFRGBAImageBegin`/RGBA use to free internal lookup tables (Map, BWmap, PALmap, ycbcr, etc.). It frees only non-NULL members and sets them to NULL.
functions.LogLuv32fromXYZ: `LogLuv32fromXYZ` encodes an XYZ color into a 32-bit LogLuv value: 16 bits for log luminance from Y, 8 bits each for u/v chroma. Use it with `XYZ[3]` and `em` rounding mode. If Y is 0/invalid or `s<=0`, it falls back to neutral u/v; u,v are clamped to 0..255.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAImageOriented: Reads a TIFF into an RGBA raster with a requested orientation. Call after `TIFFRGBAImageOK`; it initializes via `TIFFRGBAImageBegin`, fills `raster` starting at `raster + (rheight-img.height)*rwidth`, then ends. On unsupported/failed init it reports an error and returns 0.
functions.TIFFReadFromUserBuffer: Purpose: read one strile from caller-supplied raw buffer, using it as TIFF raw data. Use only on readable TIFFs and when raw uncompressed access is supported. It temporarily swaps tif raw buffer state; returns 0 on error, 1 on success.
functions.TIFFSwabLong: `TIFFSwabLong` byte-swaps one 32-bit `uint32_t` in place. Use it on a valid pointer to a 4-byte value when converting between endiannesses. It simply reverses the 4 bytes; no return value, no checks beyond the size assert.
functions.TIFFCreateDirectory: `TIFFCreateDirectory` initializes a new in-memory TIFF directory by resetting defaults and directory offsets/state (`diroff`, `nextdiroff`, `curoff`, row/strip). Use it before setting tags for a fresh directory. It always returns `0`.
functions.TIFFFieldWithTag: `TIFFFieldWithTag` looks up a `TIFFField` by tag in a `TIFF*`. Use it when you need field metadata for a known tag. If the tag exists, it returns the field; if not, it reports an internal error and returns `NULL`.
functions.LogLuv24toXYZ: Decodes a packed 24-bit LogLuv pixel into CIE XYZ. Use `XYZ[3]` as output. If luminance decodes to `<= 0`, it returns all zeros. If chroma decode fails, it falls back to neutral u/v and still computes XYZ.
functions.TIFFTileSize: `TIFFTileSize` returns the byte size of one tile for a TIFF image. Use it after TIFF setup to allocate/read tile buffers. It simply calls `TIFFTileSize64()` then casts to `tmsize_t`; if the size can’t fit, the cast helper handles it.
functions.TIFFErrorExt: `TIFFErrorExt` reports a TIFF error with an extra `thandle_t` context. Call it with `fd`, optional `module`, and printf-style `fmt/...`. It invokes the installed error handlers if present; if none are set, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFGetStrileByteCountWithErr: Returns the byte count for a given strile (strip/tile), using cached directory data. Call with a valid `TIFF*`, strile index, and optional `pbErr` to receive error status. It delegates to the internal offset/bytecount lookup helper.
functions.TIFFMergeFieldInfo: Adds a compatibility field-array to a TIFF handle. Call it with a valid `TIFF*` and an array of `TIFFFieldInfo` to register extra/custom tags. Returns `-1` on allocation failure; otherwise it appends the merged field set.
functions.TIFFReadEncodedTile: Reads one tile and decodes it into `buf`. Use with a valid `tile` index and enough space in `buf` (`size`). Returns bytes read or `-1` on error. For uncompressed tiles it may read raw data directly, then bit-reverse/postdecode if needed.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAStripExt: Design: read one full strip into an RGBA raster. Use only on non-tiled TIFFs, with `row` at the strip start (`row % RowsPerStrip == 0`). If tiled or misaligned, it errors and returns 0. `stop_on_error` controls whether RGBA decoding stops on errors.
functions.TIFFGetStrileOffset: `TIFFGetStrileOffset` returns the byte offset of a given strile (strip/tile) in a TIFF. Use it with a valid `TIFF*` and strile index. It simply forwards to `TIFFGetStrileOffsetWithErr(..., NULL)`, so any error reporting is suppressed here.
functions.TIFFRasterScanlineSize64: Returns the raster scanline size in bytes for `tif` using current directory settings. Use after tags are set. For contiguous data: width*bits/sample*spp, rounded to bytes. For separate planar data: bytes per sample scanline * spp. Uses 64-bit math.
functions.XYZtoRGB24: Converts XYZ float color to 8-bit RGB. Use with `xyz[3]` input and `rgb[3]` output. It assumes CCIR-709 primaries and gamma 2.0; each channel is clamped to 0..255, with ≤0→0 and ≥1→255.
functions.TIFFCurrentStrip: `TIFFCurrentStrip(TIFF*)` is a simple accessor that returns the library’s current strip index stored in `tif_curstrip`. Use it after TIFF I/O operations to query which strip libtiff currently tracks. It does no validation and just returns the stored value.
functions.TIFFGetWriteProc: `TIFFGetWriteProc` returns the current write callback stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to inspect which function libtiff will call for output. It doesn’t write data or change state; it simply returns `tif->tif_writeproc` (possibly `NULL` if unset).
functions.TIFFGetStrileOffsetWithErr: Returns a strile’s offset with error reporting. Call with a valid `TIFF*`, strile index, and optional `pbErr`; it uses the directory’s strip-offset entry/cache. On success returns the offset, on failure returns 0 and sets `*pbErr` if provided.
functions.LogL10fromY: `LogL10fromY` converts a luminance `Y` to a 10-bit LogL code. Use it for LogL encoding: values `>=15.742` clamp to `0x3ff`, `<=0.00024283` clamp to `0`, otherwise it computes `64*(log2(Y)+12)` and truncates via `tiff_itrunc(em)`.
functions.LogLuv24fromXYZ: Encodes XYZ to a 24-bit LogLuv value: 14-bit log-luminance + 10-bit chroma. Pass `XYZ[3]` and encoding mode `em`. If Y is zero/invalid or `s<=0`, it uses neutral u/v; if chroma encode fails, it falls back to neutral no-dither encoding.
functions.TIFFCreateGPSDirectory: `TIFFCreateGPSDirectory` creates a TIFF GPS IFD using libtiff’s built-in GPS field definitions. Call it with a valid `TIFF*`; it delegates to `TIFFCreateCustomDirectory`. It returns that function’s status, so success/failure depends on the underlying directory creation.
functions.TIFFFieldDataType: `TIFFFieldDataType` is a simple accessor: it returns the `field_type` stored in a `TIFFField`. Use it on a valid, non-NULL `TIFFField*` to query that field’s data type. It does no validation or conversion; it just returns the struct member.
functions.TIFFGetReadProc: `TIFFGetReadProc` returns the current read callback stored in a `TIFF*`. Use it to inspect the I/O read function attached to a TIFF handle. It does not read data or modify state; it simply returns `tif->tif_readproc` (or whatever callback is currently set).
functions.TIFFSwabArrayOfLong8: Swaps byte order of an array of 64-bit integers in place. Use it on `n` `uint64_t` values when TIFF data endianness differs. It always processes all `n` elements; `n==0` does nothing.
functions.TIFFFieldPassCount: `TIFFFieldPassCount` returns the `field_passcount` flag from a `TIFFField`. Use it to check whether a tag’s value is stored as a count+data pair and must be passed that way to the tag handler. It just reads the field; no extra logic or validation.
functions.TIFFWarningExt: `TIFFWarningExt` emits a formatted TIFF warning. Call it with a client handle, module name, and printf-style format. It forwards the warning to the installed warning handler(s); if none are set, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFWriteEncodedStrip: Writes an encoded strip to a TIFF. Use after setting directory/strip layout; `strip` must be valid or the strip table may grow for contiguous planar config. Returns bytes written, `-1` on error. Separate-planar images can’t grow by strips.
functions.TIFFReadCustomDirectory:
Purpose: read a TIFF directory at `diroff` using a custom field table.  
Use: call with a valid `TIFF*`, directory offset, and `infoarray`; it resets prior state, loads fields, fetches/parses the directory.  
Behavior: returns 0 on fetch/error, warns on unknown tags, and initializes `tif->tif_dir` from the custom directory.
functions.TIFFSetTagExtender: `TIFFSetTagExtender` installs a global tag-extension callback used by libtiff to let apps/libraries register extra TIFF tags. Pass a `TIFFExtendProc`; it returns the previous extender. On call, it simply replaces `_TIFFextender` with your function.
functions.TIFFFlushData: `TIFFFlushData` flushes pending written TIFF image data. Use it after writing when you want buffered data pushed out. If the TIFF hasn’t been written to yet, it returns 1. If `TIFF_POSTENCODE` is set, it runs `tif_postencode` first; failure returns 0. Otherwise it calls `TIFFFlushData1`.
functions.TIFFReadBufferSetup: Sets the read buffer for a TIFF, replacing any existing raw buffer and disabling mmap use. If `bp` is given, it uses caller memory; otherwise it allocates/zeros a rounded-up buffer and owns it. Returns 0 on invalid size, else success.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAImage: `TIFFReadRGBAImage` is a convenience wrapper that reads a TIFF into an RGBA raster. Call it with the desired output width/height, a `uint32_t*` buffer, and `stop` to control early abort on errors. It always uses `ORIENTATION_BOTLEFT` and just forwards to `TIFFReadRGBAImageOriented`.
functions.TIFFSetFileName: `TIFFSetFileName` updates a `TIFF` handle’s stored file-name string and returns the previous name. Use it to replace `tif->tif_name` with a new `const char*`. It does no copying or validation; it just assigns the pointer.
functions.TIFFCurrentRow: `TIFFCurrentRow(TIFF*)` is a simple accessor that returns the current row index stored in `tif->tif_row`. Use it to query TIFF I/O progress/state. It does no validation or side effects; it just returns the row value currently tracked by the `TIFF` handle.
functions.TIFFXYZToRGB: Converts CIE XYZ to RGB using the `TIFFCIELabToRGB` display matrix/ranges. Initialize/populate `cielab` first, then pass X/Y/Z and output pointers. It clips inputs to valid bounds, then maps to channel values; bad inputs are clamped, not rejected.
functions.TIFFReadRGBAStrip: `TIFFReadRGBAStrip` is a thin wrapper that reads one TIFF strip as RGBA into `raster`. Call it with a valid `TIFF*`, starting `row`, and output buffer. It returns whatever `TIFFReadRGBAStripExt(...,0)` returns, so success/failure follows that helper.
functions.TIFFWarning: `TIFFWarning` reports a formatted warning message. Call it with a `module` name and `printf`-style `fmt`/args. It invokes the installed warning handler(s) if present; if none are set, it does nothing.
functions.TIFFGetField: `TIFFGetField` is a varargs wrapper for `TIFFVGetField`, used to retrieve a TIFF tag’s value(s) from `tif`. Call it with the tag and pointers/receivers for that tag’s expected data. It returns the status from `TIFFVGetField` (success/failure).
functions.TIFFCurrentDirectory: `TIFFCurrentDirectory(TIFF*)` returns the current TIFF directory index stored in `tif->tif_curdir`. Use it after opening/reading a TIFF to know which directory is active. It just reports the value; it doesn’t change state or validate anything.
functions.TIFFSetClientdata: `TIFFSetClientdata` sets `tif->tif_clientdata` to `newvalue` and returns the previous value. Use it to replace the TIFF handle’s client-data pointer; it has no validation or side effects beyond the assignment.
functions.TIFFGetUnmapFileProc: Returns the TIFF handle’s current unmap callback (`tif_unmapproc`). Use it to query the function set for unmapping a mapped file. It does no work itself; it just returns the stored proc, or NULL if none is set.
functions.TIFFSetField: `TIFFSetField` is a varargs wrapper for `TIFFVSetField`. Use it to set a TIFF tag on a `TIFF*` by passing the tag and its value(s). It forwards args via `va_list` and returns `TIFFVSetField`’s status, so success/failure depends on that call.
functions.TIFFUnsetField: `TIFFUnsetField` clears a TIFF tag from the directory. Use it with a TIFF handle and tag ID. Returns 0 if the tag isn’t known; otherwise it clears the standard field bit, or removes/frees a custom tag value and shifts the custom list.
functions.TIFFReadEncodedStrip: Reads one encoded strip and decodes it into `buf`. Use with a valid `TIFF*`, strip index, and buffer; `size` is the buffer size or `-1` if unknown. Returns decoded byte count, or `-1` on error. For uncompressed strips, it may fast-path via raw read.
functions.TIFFWriteScanline: Design: write one scanline to a TIFF image, extending ImageLength if needed for contiguous data. Use with `buf`, `row`, `sample`; returns -1 on write/check errors. Separate planes reject ImageLength growth; invalid state also fails.
functions.TIFFYCbCrtoRGB:
Converts one YCbCr pixel to RGB using precomputed tables in `TIFFYCbCrToRGB`. Pass 8-bit Y/Cb/Cr values and output pointers; inputs/outputs are clamped to 0–255. It’s for per-pixel conversion, not general bit-depth YCbCr.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Do not allocate a TIFFYCbCrToRGB object with malloc and fill it with arbitrary bytes. TIFFYCbCrtoRGB expects a fully initialized conversion state whose internal lookup-table pointers (for example Y_tab, Cr_r_tab, Cb_g_tab, Cr_g_tab, Cb_b_tab) are valid. Create and initialize the structure only through libtiff’s intended setup/initialization routines, or obtain it from higher-level libtiff decoding paths that prepare YCbCr conversion state before calling TIFFYCbCrtoRGB. Ensure the object remains alive for the duration of the call, do not overwrite its fields manually, and pass only a valid initialized pointer. Y, Cb, and Cr may be arbitrary because the function clamps them, but the conversion context itself must be valid.
functions._TIFFcalloc:
`_TIFFcalloc` is a thin libtiff wrapper for `calloc`. Use it to allocate `nmemb * siz` zeroed bytes. If either argument is 0, it returns `NULL` immediately; otherwise it forwards to `calloc`, so it may also return `NULL` on allocation failure.
Yes, this is misuse. `_TIFFcalloc(nmemb, siz)` allocates exactly `nmemb * siz` bytes (or NULL if either argument is 0). Ensure the product matches the number of bytes you will later access. Do not derive `nmemb` and `siz` with truncating division unless you also use the resulting product as the true buffer size. Prefer computing `nmemb` and `siz` so that `nmemb * siz == intended_size`, or store `allocated_size = nmemb * siz` and never read/write beyond that. Also check for NULL before use.
functions.TIFFWriteTile: `TIFFWriteTile` writes one image tile at `(x,y,z,s)` from `buf`. It first validates the tile coords with `TIFFCheckTile`; on failure returns `-1`. Otherwise it computes the tile index and calls `TIFFWriteEncodedTile` with size `-1`, letting libtiff clamp to the real tile size.
functions.TIFFGetTagListCount: `TIFFGetTagListCount(TIFF*)` returns the number of custom tag values currently stored in the TIFF directory (`td_customValueCount`). Use it to query how many custom tags/values are present; it just reads the count and does no validation or modification.
functions.TIFFDataWidth: `TIFFDataWidth(type)` returns the byte width of a TIFF field type for size/offset calculations. Use it to map a `TIFFDataType` to 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes. Unknown/unsupported types return 0; `0` and byte/ASCII/undefined are 1.
